title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: The paper addresses unsupervised anomaly detection on datasets with heterogeneous local densities, where global distance-based methods miss local outliers and density-based methods are quadratic-time and parameter-sensitive. It proposes SVEAD, which builds an ensemble of t random Voronoi partitions by uniformly sampling m anchor points per partition, assigns each point to its nearest anchor, and scores it within its cell as (delta/delta_max)*delta_mean (relative position normalized by cell radius, weighted by mean cell distance as a density proxy), averaging scores across the ensemble. On 45 ADBench benchmark datasets, SVEAD reportedly achieves the best average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 13 methods, with linear time and constant space complexity.

match_target.why: User hint explicitly targets Table 4 SVEAD AUC-ROC on cardio. It is the cheapest probe of the paper's central claim (SVEAD's dual-factor Voronoi scoring is state-of-the-art on ADBench): one 1,831-point dataset, CPU-only, seconds per run, no training. Honesty note for the reproducer: on cardio the paper itself shows IDK (0.9531) and iNNE (0.9447) above SVEAD's 0.9339; the target is SVEAD's reported value, not superiority on this specific dataset.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: the paper reports a std over repeated runs for exactly this target value (Table 5, cardio, VEAD: std 0.0063 over 5 runs). Band = 3 x 0.0063 = 0.0189 in AUC fraction units, kept at the 4-decimal precision the paper prints. Although AUC is bounded, Rule 1 takes precedence over Rules 2/3.

requirements.stmt: For each of t partitions, sample m anchors uniformly from the full dataset X (including anomalies) WITHOUT replacement; anchors are data points themselves.
requirements.quote: we randomly sample m points from the dataset X without replacement to form an anchor set

requirements.stmt: Cell membership is determined purely by nearest-anchor queries under Euclidean distance; no explicit Voronoi diagram (boundaries/vertices) is constructed.
requirements.quote: Each point x ∈X is assigned to its nearest anchor

requirements.stmt: Within-cell score must be the dual-factor product s(x) = (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean, where delta is distance to the assigned anchor, delta_max the maximum anchor-distance within the cell, delta_mean the mean anchor-distance within the cell (Eq. 2-3).
requirements.quote: the first term δ/δmax normalizes the distance by the maximum cell radius

requirements.stmt: If a cell contains only its anchor (|Ci| = 1), skip scoring for that point in that partition rather than dividing by delta_max = 0.
requirements.quote: we skip scoring for this point in this partition and rely on the other t −1 partitions

requirements.stmt: Final anomaly score is the arithmetic mean of the per-partition scores across the t partitions (Eq. 5); higher score = more anomalous.
requirements.quote: The final anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean

requirements.stmt: Hyperparameters for SVEAD (and iForest, iNNE, IDK): subsample/anchor count m grid-searched over {2^1,...,2^8} (printed in the PDF as {21, 22, ..., 28}; superscripts are lost in text extraction), with ensemble size t fixed at 100.
requirements.quote: the number of sample points is searched over {21, 22, . . . , 28}, with ensemble size fixed at 100

requirements.stmt: Evaluation is fully unsupervised: the model scores all data without labels; labels are used only afterwards to compute AUC-ROC/AUC-PR.
requirements.quote: the labels are used to compute the AUC-ROC and AUC-PR for each dataset only after the models have made predictions

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 5 times (different random anchor draws) and report the mean; Tables 5 and 7 give the corresponding standard deviations.
requirements.cite: Section 5.1 'Evaluation Metrics'; Appendix D note before Tables 4-7
requirements.quote: For each dataset and method, we repeat experiments 5 times and report the average performance.

requirements.stmt: Use the ADBench versions of the 45 real-world datasets; for cardio: 1,831 samples x 21 features, 176 anomalies (9.61%), per Table 3.
requirements.quote: We evaluate SVEAD on 45 publicly available benchmark datasets widely used in anomaly detection from ADBench (Han et al., 2022).

requirements.stmt: For reproducing comparison columns: load LOF, iForest, iNNE, IDK, ECOD, COPOD, DeepSVDD, AE etc. from PyOD; take SLAD and DTE from their official repositories.
requirements.quote: Most algorithms are implemented from the PyOD library (Zhao et al., 2019), while SLAD and DTE are obtained from their official repositories.

requirements.stmt: For baseline parity: LOF's neighborhood size k grid is {5, 10, 20, 40}; ECOD and COPOD run with defaults (deterministic, zero variance); deep methods use original-paper defaults.
requirements.quote: LOF's neighborhood size k is searched over {5, 10, 20, 40}
